def is_safe_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when `name` is a single plain file name: non-empty, not "." or "..",
    and containing no "/", no "\\" and no NUL character, so it cannot leave `notes`."""
    ex is_safe_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_safe_name("") == False
    ex is_safe_name(".") == False
    ex is_safe_name("..") == False
    ex is_safe_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_safe_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a/b.txt") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a\\b.txt") == False
    if name == "" or name == "." or name == "..":
        return False
    if "/" in name or "\\" in name or "\0" in name:
        return False
    return True

def read_note(name: str) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the file `name` inside the directory `notes`, or "" if it is missing,
    unreadable, or the name is not safe (see is_safe_name).
    The read happens inside `with fs = fs.sub("notes")`, so `fs` cannot reach outside `notes`."""
    post is_safe_name(name) or out == ""
    if not is_safe_name(name):
        return ""
    text = ""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        text = fs.read(name) else ""
    return text
